theory.intro: Two triangles are **similar** when one is an enlargement of the other: same shape, every side scaled by the same factor. Four tests decide similarity, and you must write the full reasoning every time.
facts: The scale factor is $\frac{\text{image}}{\text{original}}$ — divide a side of the second triangle by its matching side in the first.
steps: Pair up corresponding parts: shortest side with shortest side, largest angle with largest angle.
For the side tests, divide each side of one triangle by its corresponding side in the other and compare the ratios.

Match the pattern to a test — equiangular (AAA), SSS, SAS or RHS — to prove similarity. If no test can be established, the information may be insufficient. Conclude that triangles are not similar only when the givens disprove similarity: their complete angle sets differ, or, after establishing correspondence, corresponding side ratios differ.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\angle A=\angle E=60^\circ$ and $\angle B=\angle F=60^\circ$.

At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so the triangles are similar (AAA).

Matching $A$ with $E$, $B$ with $F$ and $C$ with $D$ gives $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle EFD$. All angles are equal, so other consistent vertex orders are also valid.

Match the shortest sides and the two longer equal sides.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{GH}{AB}&=\frac{13.5}{9}=1.5\\\frac{GI}{AC}&=\frac{13.5}{9}=1.5\\\frac{HI}{BC}&=\frac{6}{4}=1.5\end{aligned}$

Three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ (SSS).

For $\triangle DEF$ compared with $\triangle ABC$, the equal-side ratio is $\frac{3.6}{9}=0.4$, but the base ratio is $\frac{1.7}{4}=0.425$. These differ, so $\triangle DEF$ is not similar to either of the other triangles.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{DE}{AB}&=\frac{9}{6}=1.5\\\frac{EF}{BC}&=\frac{13.5}{9}=1.5\end{aligned}$

Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles $\angle ABC$ and $\angle DEF$ are both $60^\circ$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (SAS).

The scale factor is $\frac{\text{image}}{\text{original}}=\frac{9}{6}=1.5$.

Both triangles are right-angled. The hypotenuses are $AC$ and $DF$, opposite the right angles.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{DF}{AC}&=\frac{15}{10}=1.5\\\frac{DE}{AB}&=\frac{12}{8}=1.5\end{aligned}$

The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (RHS).

workedExamples.question_text:
Use the angle sum of a triangle to decide whether each pair is similar. Give full reasoning.

(a) $\triangle ABC$ has $\angle A=48^\circ$ and $\angle B=72^\circ$. $\triangle DEF$ has $\angle D=60^\circ$ and $\angle E=48^\circ$.

(b) $\triangle PQR$ has $\angle P=48^\circ$ and $\angle Q=72^\circ$. $\triangle STU$ has $\angle S=48^\circ$ and $\angle T=82^\circ$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)

$\begin{aligned}\angle C&=180^\circ-48^\circ-72^\circ\\&=60^\circ\\\angle F&=180^\circ-60^\circ-48^\circ\\&=72^\circ\end{aligned}$

Both triangles have angles $48^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $72^\circ$. At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle EFD$ (AAA).

(b)

$\begin{aligned}\angle R&=180^\circ-48^\circ-72^\circ\\&=60^\circ\\\angle U&=180^\circ-48^\circ-82^\circ\\&=50^\circ\end{aligned}$

The complete angle sets are $48^\circ,72^\circ,60^\circ$ and $48^\circ,82^\circ,50^\circ$. They differ, so the triangles are not similar.

In $\triangle ABC$, the base angles are equal.

$\begin{aligned}\angle B=\angle C&=\frac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}\\&=30^\circ\end{aligned}$

In $\triangle DEF$, the base angles are equal, so $\angle E=\angle F=30^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle D&=180^\circ-30^\circ-30^\circ\\&=120^\circ\end{aligned}$

At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (AAA).

development.question_text:
Two of these three triangles are similar.
In $\Delta ABC$, $AB=2.4$, $BC=3.6$ and $\angle ABC=120^{\circ}$.
In $\Delta DEF$, $DE=4$, $EF=6$ and $\angle DEF=120^{\circ}$.
In $\Delta GHI$, $GH=3$, $HI=5$ and $\angle GHI=120^{\circ}$.
Choose the similar pair, state the test, and write a similarity statement.
development.solution_text:
Match the equal included angles $B$ and $E$, with $AB$ corresponding to $DE$ and $BC$ to $EF$.
$\frac{4}{2.4}=\frac{5}{3}$
$\frac{6}{3.6}=\frac{5}{3}$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles ($120^{\circ}$) are equal.
$\Delta ABC\ |||\ \Delta DEF$ (SAS).
Each triangle has only one obtuse angle, so any similarity must match the $120^{\circ}$ vertices. The shorter and longer sides meeting that angle must correspond. Their ratios within each triangle are $\frac{2.4}{3.6}=\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{3}{5}$, so $\Delta GHI$ is not similar to either of the others.

Left triangle: angles are $55^{\circ}$, $60^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=65^{\circ}$.
Right triangle: angles are $55^{\circ}$, $70^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}-70^{\circ}=55^{\circ}$.
Only one pair of corresponding angles ($55^{\circ}$) is equal, and the equiangular test needs at least two pairs.
The triangles are not similar.

Left triangle: third angle $= 180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$.
Right triangle: third angle $= 180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} = 65^{\circ}$.
Both triangles have angles $40^{\circ}$, $65^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$.
There are at least two pairs of equal corresponding angles, so the triangles are similar (equiangular, AAA).

$\frac{6}{3}=2$
$\frac{10}{5}=2$
$\frac{12}{6}=2$
For $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta DEF$, three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio; the sides of $\Delta GHI$ ($4$, $6$, $7$) do not share a common ratio with either triangle.
$\Delta ABC\ |||\ \Delta DEF$ (SSS).

Match equal angles: $\angle A = \angle E = 75^{\circ}$, $\angle B = \angle F = 55^{\circ}$, so the third vertices $C$ and $D$ also match.
There are at least two pairs of equal corresponding angles.
$\Delta ABC\ |||\ \Delta EFD$ (equiangular, AAA).

development.question_text:
In $\Delta ABC$, $\angle B=90^{\circ}$, $AC=17$ and $AB=8$.
In $\Delta DEF$, $\angle E=90^{\circ}$, $DF=42.5$ and $DE=20$.
Identify why the two triangles are similar. Write the full reasoning.
development.solution_text:
Both triangles are right-angled. The hypotenuses are $AC$ and $DF$, opposite the right angles.
Match $AC$ with $DF$ and $AB$ with $DE$.
$\frac{42.5}{17}=2.5$
$\frac{20}{8}=2.5$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so the triangles are similar (RHS).

$\frac{6}{4}=1.5$
$\frac{15}{10}=1.5$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles ($35^{\circ}$) are equal, so the triangles are similar (SAS).
The scale factor is $1.5$.

mastery.solution_text:
Left triangle: the base angles are equal, so each is $\frac{180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}}{2}=25^{\circ}$.
Right triangle: both base angles are $25^{\circ}$, so the apex angle is $180^{\circ}-25^{\circ}-25^{\circ}=130^{\circ}$.
Both triangles have angles $25^{\circ}$, $25^{\circ}$ and $130^{\circ}$.
There are at least two pairs of equal corresponding angles, so the triangles are similar (equiangular, AAA).

mastery.question_text:
Two of these three isosceles triangles are similar.
In $\Delta ABC$, $AB=AC=7.5$ and $BC=3$.
In $\Delta DEF$, $DE=DF=2.52$ and $EF=1.02$.
In $\Delta GHI$, $GH=GI=4.5$ and $HI=1.8$.
Choose the similar pair, state the test, and write a similarity statement.
mastery.solution_text:
Match sides in size order: the base is the shortest side in each triangle, and the two equal sides are the longer sides.
$\frac{GH}{AB}=\frac{4.5}{7.5}=0.6$
$\frac{GI}{AC}=\frac{4.5}{7.5}=0.6$
$\frac{HI}{BC}=\frac{1.8}{3}=0.6$
Three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\Delta ABC\ |||\ \Delta GHI$ (SSS).
For $\Delta DEF$ compared with $\Delta ABC$, the equal-side ratio is $\frac{2.52}{7.5}=0.336$ but the base ratio is $\frac{1.02}{3}=0.34$. These differ, so $\Delta DEF$ is not similar to $\Delta ABC$ or its similar triangle $\Delta GHI$.

The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle: $13$ in the first triangle and $19.5$ in the second.
$\frac{19.5}{13}=1.5$
$\frac{7.5}{5}=1.5$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so the triangles are similar (RHS).
